purpose: Historical evidence for new original model geometry; no source photos used as runtime textures.

distinctions.observations: Directly observed in the listed period source.
distinctions.adaptations: Authored game simplification; not a historical measurement.
distinctions.dimensions: New prop dimensions and even-length partition placement are authored against existing native shells.
distinctions.uncertainty: Complete Administration rear/upper office and New York upper subdivision plans were not inspected. No Fisheries interior photograph was verified.

sources.title: Report of the Board of General Managers of the Exhibit of the State of New York at the Worlds Columbian Exposition
sources.creator: New York State Board of General Managers
observations: Pillared hall serves side rooms and stair; ground post/telegraph and service offices.
Upper central banquet/reception/ball room; Board of Women Managers on right, General Managers on left.
Pompeian orange-red stair panels, cream/gold banquet hall, Renaissance marble chimneypieces, antique French/Italian furnishings, carpets and electric fixtures.
adaptations: Native-grid partitions and existing relocated game stair.
Original simplified carved seating, marble surround, electric globes and coffer/panel motifs; no exact tapestry or Millet mural reproduction.
sources.rights: 1894 US publication, public domain; IA/LOC catalogue records no known restrictions.

sources.title: Banquet Hall photograph in New York report
sources.creator: Photographer uncredited in the inspected plate
sources.locator: One-based PDF scan163, facing printed p.100
observations: Tall arched and decorated hall, repeated wall panels, cornices and electric pendant lighting.
adaptations: Flat native-level coffer set and repeated wall panels simplify the curved ornamental ceiling.
Banquet table arrangement is optional new set dressing, not the photographed floor layout.

sources.title: McKim, Mead and White New York State Building first-floor plan
sources.creator: McKim, Mead and White
observations: First-floor named side rooms and central hall adjacency.
adaptations: Partition lines quantized to the already accepted48m shell; game access stair position retained.
sources.rights: See preserved source registry; no new image or license claim introduced.

sources.title: Administration Building front-half ground-floor plan
sources.creator: Richard Morris Hunt / A. Riquois
observations: Source-labeled public, post, exchange, information, foreign visitors, ambulance, doctor and pharmacy functions.
adaptations: Existing ground front partitions retained. Furnishings inferred from room use. Rear and upper office subdivisions interpreted.
sources.rights: See preserved original-source registry; no new photo-texture import.

sources.title: Interior of dome of Administration Building
sources.creator: C.D. Arnold, photographer; R.M. Hunt, architect
observations: Repeated cartouches, panels, gilded architectural ornament and dome decorations.
adaptations: Only general classical panel language informed the original geometry; no archive pixels redistributed. No Administration office photograph was inspected.
sources.rights: AIC catalogue requests contacting Ryerson and Burnham Archives for publication; image stays ignored private research.

sources.title: The Orange Tower
sources.creator: Rand, McNally and Company; photographer uncredited
sources.locator: Columbian Exposition Album, one-based PDF scan84
observations: California orange-covered tower, stepped base, arched recess, display signs and long rows of specimen fruit tables.
adaptations: Tower height6.25m and footprint authored to fit current native hall; no perspective-derived measurement. Simplified spheres, tiers and label.
Botanical cases and stand arrangements are period interpretations.

sources.title: Under the Central Dome of the Horticultural Building
sources.creator: Rand, McNally and Company; photographer uncredited
sources.locator: Columbian Exposition Album, one-based PDF scan114
observations: Rocky mound planted with tropical vegetation and Mammoth Crystal Cave entrance; caption describes a reproduction of a South Dakota cave chamber.
adaptations: Original hollow low-poly rock chamber, entrance arch, crystal points and ferns. No geological survey or exact cave arrangement.
Replaces only the two listed central source palms; surrounding planting remains.

sources.title: Horticultural Building floor and gallery diagram
sources.creator: W.B. Conkey Company
observations: Galleries, open courts and gallery cafe functions.
adaptations: End-corner potting rooms and low fruit installation dividers are authored; no exact historical service-room survey.

sources.title: The Aquarium of the United States Fish Commission at the Worlds Columbian Exposition
sources.creator: S.A. Forbes
observations: Two concentric tank rings, outer attendant passage, darkened spectator aisle and double-faced inner tanks.
Central pool26ft across; two public ring aisles about15ft wide.
50 tanks:24small +16large outer;8ordinary +1double +1long inner. Visually verified16; OCR18 was rejected.
adaptations: 40 outer and10 simplified equal inner bays. Original unequal inner dimensions, vaulted aisle cover, detailed plumbing and hidden service ladders omitted.
Original native pavilion unchanged; pool is an above-floor prop with no new basement.
sources.rights: Contemporary US government publication, public domain.

sources.creator: W.B. Conkey Company
sources.locator: Plans and Diagrams of All Exhibit Buildings: one-based scans35main,36gallery,37angling
observations: Radial angling installation divisions, main floor and gallery.
adaptations: 12m native radial runs, rod cases, boats and nets. Exact exhibit allocation and object dimensions authored.
